input.title: auth.renown.source chooses whether credential checks query a remote Renown (remote, the default) or this switchboard's own renown-read-model subgraph in-process (self)

input.description: Env overrides win field by field (RENOWN_SOURCE, RENOWN_URL, SWITCHBOARD_URL). remote tries switchboardUrl, discovery via url, then the REST API; self needs the renown package loaded or startup fails.

metadata.reason: Extracted from apps/switchboard/Auth.md at v6.2.2-dev.74 — 'Which Renown Instance Is Used' and 'The Switchboard's Own Identity'
Configures which instance performs the credential existence check that the verification pipeline depends on

input.content:
```json
{ "auth": { "enabled": true, "admins": ["0x111"],
            "renown": { "source": "remote", "url": "https://renown.acme.io", "switchboardUrl": "https://sb.acme.io/graphql" } } }
```

| Field | Env override | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `RENOWN_SOURCE` | `remote` (default) queries another instance; `self` reads this switchboard's own `renown-read-model` subgraph in-process |
| `url` | `RENOWN_URL` | Renown base URL for discovery and the REST fallback; defaults to `https://www.renown.id` |
| `switchboardUrl` | `SWITCHBOARD_URL` | A switchboard GraphQL endpoint to read credentials from directly, skipping discovery |

Env vars win over the config file **field by field**, and a blank value counts as unset. With `source: "remote"` the order is `switchboardUrl`, then discovery via `url`, then the Renown REST API at `url`. With `source: "self"` both URLs are ignored for verification, but `url` still applies to the switchboard's own identity.

`self` requires a loaded package that provides the `renown-read-model` subgraph (`@powerhousedao/renown-package`); **startup fails if none does**, rather than booting a switchboard that rejects every authenticated request. The layering keeps core ignorant of Renown: `@renown/sdk` owns the read-model contract (`RENOWN_READ_MODEL_SUBGRAPH`, `createLocalCredentialVerifier`), the switchboard app wires it to the running reactor after the API is up, and `reactor-api` only supplies the generic `GraphQLManager.executeSubgraphQuery` plus an injectable `verifyCredential`. A host that sets `self` without injecting a verifier is refused at boot rather than silently verified against a remote Renown.

Separately, a switchboard has its **own identity** — the `ph login` keypair it uses to authenticate *outbound* to remote drives and services. It authenticates against `auth.renown.url` too, so one setting covers both directions; `identity.baseUrl` at startup points it elsewhere, and unset everywhere it falls back to `https://www.renown.id`.

_Source: apps/switchboard/Auth.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.74)._
